correctness.rationale: For binary input/output, each state output action is identity or flip and inverse-input reachability is a permutation iff delta0(A)=delta1(A), A=set of flippers. With d=delta1 and pi=d^-1 delta0 this becomes pi(A)=A: a bijection, giving choose(n,k)*n!*k!*(n-k)!=(n!)^2 machines for each |A|=k. Under state-only relabeling, Burnside fixes d and pi in centralizer C(sigma), and invariant A is a union of orbits of permutation pi on cycles of sigma. The cycle-index identity sum_tau prod_C (1+s^{|C|})=m!sum_{h=0}^m s^h gives U_n(t)=sum_{lambda partition n}prod_j j^{m_j}m_j!sum_{h=0}^{m_j}t^{jh}. Permutation transition orbits are SCCs; labeled SET construction yields n!*[z^n t^k]log F(z,t), with F=sum_n n!(sum_{k<=n}t^k)z^n. The unlabeled multiset inversion is V=sum_{r>=1}mu(r)/r log U(z^r,t^r). For uniform labeled machines, d uniform and pi weighted 2^{cycles}; common invariant j-subset expectation (j+1)(n-j+1)/((n+1)*C(n,j)), and union bound/Bonferroni yield connected probability 1-2/n+O(n^-2). Independently tested all (n!)^2*2^n raw pairs n<=4 under direct inverse-transition definitions and connected reachability: total 2,12,144,2880; connected 2,8,88,1776. No infinite conclusion drawn solely from experiments.
